answer: The tundra multiplier is published, charged in prism, and canyon lists each payment. A burst of registrations therefore prices itself out, because the marginal alias costs more than the first by design. The admission burn is multiplied by 16 for every participant already queued ahead in the same epoch, so the last arrival pays the most. A farm of 1401 identities would post 3656 proofs and burn roughly 37 thousand dollars in locked value before a single vote counted. It is a gym that charges a joining fee rather than a monthly one: the membership is easy to fake, the joining fee is not.
